items.t: Kitsilano is an official City of Vancouver local area (one of the City's 22), running along the south shore of English Bay between Granville Island and Point Grey; the City's history text refers to the area from Burrard to Alma Streets — exact boundary roads from a City source: Not verified.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the West 4th Avenue corridor (Kits West, Star of Kitsilano, Avanti, Jade West and Delano all sit on West 4th), plus the Marstrand Avenue / Point Grey Road side at the north-west (Solo at Hadden Park / Vanier Park edge), with further apartment stock along the Cornwall and Broadway edges. The interior streets are single detached houses, duplexes and multiple dwellings under the RT-7 / RT-8 and R1-1 schedules.

Retail corridors: the City names extensive restaurants and retail along West 4th Avenue and West Broadway, and calls Kitsilano one of the city's organic-food hubs. Kitsilano Beach Park is at 1499 Arbutus Street.

Transit: no SkyTrain station sits inside Kitsilano. Bus routes on the West 4th / Broadway / Cornwall corridors include the 2, 4, 7, 9, 14, 44, 84 and the 99 B-Line; the Broadway Subway is extending the Millennium Line along Broadway at the area's south edge.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Kitsilano

items.t: Area plan: the Broadway Plan covers Vine Street to Clark Drive and 1st Avenue to 16th Avenue, including parts of Kitsilano, and is the framework tied to the Broadway Subway; a Kitsilano-specific community plan: Not verified.

Coastal flood: the City's Coastal Flood Risk Assessment covers a Point Grey–Kitsilano study area — the shoreline from Point Grey to Kitsilano Point faces the Strait of Georgia, is exposed to waves from the northwest, flood protection is limited and riprap west of Kitsilano Beach is discontinuous; the Province advises planning for 0.5 m of sea level rise by 2050 and 1 m by 2100. Relevant to the beach-side low-rises; parcel-level status: Not verified.

blocks.text: Good to know about Kitsilano

items.t: West 4th Avenue is the whole condo map.

A 129-unit supportive-housing project was approved inside Kitsilano. Council approved the rezoning at 2086–2098 West 7th Avenue and 2091 West 8th Avenue — 129 studio homes — on July 27, 2022. Buyers on the West 7th / 8th blocks should know the project is approved, not rumoured.
The Broadway Plan stops at 1st Avenue.

Delano's roof is dated in its own listings. Listing copy records a new roof in 2018 for the 1996 Delano building — a checkable capital fact that belongs in any fee comparison against Star of Kitsilano (also 1996) across the corridor.

At 7 storeys and 176 units (LMS3170, 1998, Intergulf) it is an outlier among the 50–84-unit wood-frame low-rises — its depreciation report and CRF comparison set is concrete-building issues (parkade, elevators), not the wood-frame envelope cycle of its West 4th neighbours.

Kitsilano Secondary's name in a listing is not a catchment promise. Four elementaries and the secondary sit inside the area, but SD39 catchments are address-based; the one verified locator run (3505 West 7th Ave) returned Bayview Elementary and Kitsilano Secondary for that address only.

items.t: Kitsilano is an official City of Vancouver local area — one of the City's 22 distinct areas — running along the south shore of English Bay between Granville Island and Point Grey; the City's history text refers to the area from Burrard to Alma Streets.
Nearby areas: Point Grey to the west, Fairview across Burrard Street to the east, South Granville / Shaughnessy to the south-east, Arbutus Ridge and Dunbar-Southlands to the south.

Transit and roads: bus routes on the West 4th Avenue / West Broadway / Cornwall corridors include the 2, 4, 7, 9, 14, 44, 84 and the 99 B-Line; no SkyTrain station or bus exchange sits inside Kitsilano — the Broadway Subway is extending the Millennium Line along the Broadway corridor at the area's south edge. West 4th Avenue and West Broadway are the retail corridors, and the Burrard Bridge links the area's east end downtown.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based. Schools located in Kitsilano: Bayview Elementary, 3505 West 7th Avenue; Gordon Elementary, 2268 Bayswater Street; Hudson Elementary, 1530 Maple Street; Tennyson Elementary, 2650 Maple Street; and Kitsilano Secondary, 2706 Trafalgar Street.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Kitsilano

items.t: Form B diligence (all 5 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern. For the 1979–1999 stock (Old Kits Townhomes, Bayside Manor, Yorkville Mews, Kits Palisades), the depreciation report and CRF balance are the diligence centre of the purchase.

blocks.text: Good to know about Kitsilano

items.t: There was a salmon cannery at the foot of Macdonald Street. The City's history records that at the turn of the century the area from Burrard to Alma was dense forest despite earlier logging, and a canning factory at the foot of Macdonald Street once could not cope with the "hundreds of thousands of salmon" caught in 1900 — the beach blocks were industrial waterfront within living memory of the oldest houses.

Kits Beach's official name and address rarely appear in listings. Kitsilano Beach Park is at 1499 Arbutus Street, and the City repeats the travel-magazine line that Kits Beach is among the "top 10 best city beaches in the world" — the park, not the sand alone, is the amenity the north-of-4th townhouse premium is buying.

A supportive-housing rezoning already reshaped one south-Kits block. Council approved 129 studio homes at 2086–2098 West 7th Avenue and 2091 West 8th Avenue on July 27, 2022 — south-edge buyers near West 7th and Vine should know the block's form changed by rezoning, not by the Broadway Plan.

The library is on Macdonald, not on 4th. The Kitsilano Branch of Vancouver Public Library sits at 2425 MacDonald Street — mid-neighbourhood, serving the residential streets where the townhouse clusters actually are.
The confirmed recreation anchor in the sources read is Kitsilano Beach Park itself — a buyer mapping amenities should treat the beach park, not a community centre, as the verified in-area facility.

No hospital sits inside Kitsilano. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is the hospital named on the health-authority location page east of the area — "close to VGH" in listing copy means a drive across Burrard, not a walk.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Kitsilano
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Interior-street lots: single detached houses, duplexes and multiple dwellings under R1-1, RT-7 and RT-8, with strata apartment stock along the West 4th Avenue, Cornwall and Broadway edges. The RT schedules' stated intent is to encourage retention and renovation of buildings consistent with the historical character of the area — the defining land fact in Kitsilano. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees. The strata-versus-freehold split by street is not verified.

Lot character: the RT-8 schedule states a minimum site area of 306 m² for a duplex; R1-1 minimums run 306 m² (3–4-unit multiple dwellings) through 464 m² (5 units) to 557 m² (6 or more units), with secondary suites and laneway houses in the forms the schedules state. These are schedule minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel.
Serviced position: Kitsilano homes are on City water and sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a Kitsilano house confirmed on a City source is not verified.
ALR vs non-ALR: ALR land in Kitsilano is not verified — no ALR parcel is confirmed and no split is stated.

Shoreline position: the City's Coastal Flood Risk Assessment covers a Point Grey–Kitsilano study area — the shoreline from Point Grey to Kitsilano Point faces the Strait of Georgia, is exposed to waves from the northwest, flood protection is limited and riprap west of Kitsilano Beach is discontinuous; the Province advises planning for 0.5 m of sea level rise by 2050 and 1 m by 2100.

Kitsilano Beach Park is at 1499 Arbutus Street.

Transit: no SkyTrain station or bus exchange sits inside Kitsilano — bus routes on the West 4th / Broadway / Cornwall corridors include the 2, 4, 7, 9, 14, 44, 84 and the 99 B-Line; the Broadway Subway is extending the Millennium Line along Broadway at the area's south edge. Civic anchors: Kitsilano Branch, Vancouver Public Library, 2425 MacDonald Street. blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Kitsilano

items.t: Zoning — Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575, RT-7 / RT-8 and R1-1 District Schedules: the RT areas sit under RT-7 and RT-8 — RT-8 states a 306 m² minimum site area for a duplex, and the schedules' intent is retention and renovation of buildings consistent with the area's historical character; house lots elsewhere sit under R1-1 (306 m² for 3–4-unit multiple dwellings, 464 m² for 5 units, 557 m² for 6 or more units, with secondary suites and laneway houses as the schedules state). Parcel-level zone: Not verified — confirm the exact district schedule and any character-house rules before pricing a lot on multiplex value.

Plan — the Broadway Plan: covers 1st to 16th Avenue from Vine Street to Clark Drive, including parts of Kitsilano, tied to the Broadway Subway — the land-use frame for the area's south edge only; the beach blocks north of 1st Avenue are outside it.

Coastal flood diligence: the Point Grey–Kitsilano shoreline is exposed to northwest waves with limited, discontinuous flood protection, and provincial guidance plans for 0.5 m of sea-level rise by 2050 and 1 m by 2100 — get the parcel-level flood and insurance picture early on any beach-side lot.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Kitsilano ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

There was a salmon cannery at the foot of Macdonald Street: the City's history records that at the turn of the century the area from Burrard to Alma was dense forest despite earlier logging, and a canning factory at the foot of Macdonald Street once could not cope with the "hundreds of thousands of salmon" caught in 1900 — the beach blocks were industrial waterfront within living memory of the oldest houses, which is part of why the RT character-retention schedules exist.

Kits Beach's official address rarely appears in listings: Kitsilano Beach Park is at 1499 Arbutus Street, and the City repeats the travel-magazine line that Kits Beach is among the "top 10 best city beaches in the world" — the park, not the sand alone, is the amenity the north-of-4th lot premium is buying.

A supportive-housing rezoning already reshaped one south-Kits block (July 27, 2022): Council approved 129 studio homes at 2086–2098 West 7th Avenue and 2091 West 8th Avenue — south-edge lot buyers near West 7th and Vine should know the block's form changed by a site-specific rezoning, not by the Broadway Plan.

items.t: The usual duplex form: Kitsilano's RT areas sit under the RT-7 and RT-8 District Schedules of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — the RT-8 schedule states a minimum site area of 306 m² for a duplex, and the RT-7 / RT-8 intent is to encourage retention and renovation of buildings consistent with the historical character of the area; house lots elsewhere sit under R1-1 (minimums 306 m² for 3–4 units through 464 m² for 5 units to 557 m² for 6 or more units). The form class is individual duplex buildings on interior-street lots built and kept under those schedules — character-retention is part of the frame, so exterior alterations can face the schedule's intent as well as any strata approval. A specific duplex is verified on its title (one lot, strata plan, or subdivided pair); the split of freehold vs strata by street is not verified.

faq.a: Mostly 4-storey wood-frame low-rises from 1996–2013 on West 4th Avenue (Kits West, Star of Kitsilano, Avanti, Delano), one older freehold strata (Jade West, 1988), and one concrete mid-rise (Solo, 1998, 176 units). There are no condo towers in the verified stock.
faq.q: What kind of condo stock does Kitsilano actually have?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and Kits West is described in listings as rental-friendly. Short-term rentals are different: a strata bylaw can still restrict them, and Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax declaration applies to a unit left empty.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Kitsilano condo?

faq.a: The property-manager source says 2013; a current MLS® listing says 2014. flags the conflict rather than resolving it — the strata plan (EPS1696) registration record is the definitive check.
faq.q: Why do sources disagree on Kits West's build year?

faq.a: The depreciation report: stratas with 5+ lots must have one every five years (no deferral vote since July 1, 2024) and must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF. At Delano, listings note a new roof in 2018 — ask what envelope, deck and plumbing items remain in the report, not just what is done.
faq.q: What should I check in a 1990s Kits wood-frame building?

faq.a: SD39 catchments are address-based, with no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12). Run the building's exact address.
faq.q: Which schools serve a Kitsilano condo?

faq.a: Five verified strata complexes: Kits Palisades (2119 Yew Street, 1999), Bayside Manor (1659 Balsam Street, 1983), Old Kits Townhomes (1620 Balsam Street, 1979), Yorkville Mews (1848 West 1st Avenue, 1986) and Kits Quartet (3120 West 11th Avenue, 2026). Small clusters, mostly 1979–1999 wood-frame — nothing like a suburban townhouse subdivision.
faq.q: What townhouse stock does Kitsilano actually have?

faq.a: Both forms appear at the one address: the property manager describes a 12-unit townhouse complex, one current listing records a townhouse unit with strata fees, and another unit at 2119 Yew Street is MLS-classified as an apartment. Confirm the specific unit's form and strata lot on the Form B before comparing it to either stock.
faq.q: Is Kits Palisades a townhouse complex or a condo building?

faq.a: Not confirmed: the listing's building details say 4 units in the development; the listing copy says six townhomes. The disclosure statement and strata plan settle it — do not quote either figure as fact until they are read.
faq.q: How many homes are in Kits Quartet — four or six?

faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. The interior-street duplex stock here is freehold product that ordinarily sells whole. Check the title first.
faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex in Kitsilano?

faq.a: None verified. The duplex evidence here is the form class under the RT-7 / RT-8 and R1-1 schedules.
